page.layout: One printed page (p. 44) with its running text in one column. Page number at the head. No running head, no marginal notes, no catchword. The strip at the right edge is the cut-off edge of the facing page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: verum subordinationem & coordinationem vult independenter ab ipsis, non enim suæ voli-tionis Deus causam impulsivam, exemplarem vel finalem externam habet, sed Deus ipse, eiusque voluntas est prima ac unica suæ volitionis causa impulsiva, exemplaris & finalis; cum enim divina voluntas sit ipsamet Dei essentia, causam nullatenus habere potest.
VIII. Res malæ circa quas divina voluntas versatur sunt etiam summe malæ vel non summe malæ.[?]

IX. Rem summe malam seu summum malum Deus nullatenus velle potest, ideoque summum malum simpliciter est impossibile, intel-lige summum malum non in certo genere, sed simpliciter, omni modo gradu[?] tale; Nam Deus T. O. M. ut necessario amat summum bonum, sic necessario summum malum odit.

X. Res malæ quæ non sunt summe tales vel sunt mala culpæ vel pœnæ. Malum culpæ est illegalitas seu peccatum, id est, incongruentia cum norma agendi, adeoque cum voluntate & lege summa, scilicet, Dei: Etsi autem Deus peccata non potest velle voluntate approbationis, secus non essent peccata, attamen potest ea velle voluntate executionis, non

page.notes: Ornament and number "44" at the head are taken as page furniture. The stain near "voluntas" in VIII overlaps "summe malæ" and "vel non summe": the readings there are doubtful, so the paragraph is marked [?]. "gradu" in IX has a doubtful final mark. The word broken as "intel-lige" is read from the line end and may be "intellige". The strip at the right edge is text from the facing page and is not part of this page.
